Flavio: Italian, Spanish and Portuguese, from Latin Flavius, a Roman family name meaning 'golden' or 'yellow-haired'.
Isaline: French, a modern form built on Isa- (as in Isabelle or Isaac) with the suffix -line. Probably linked to Isabelle, ultimately Hebrew 'God is my oath'.
Tiziano: Italian form of Latin Titianus, 'of Titus'. Famous through the painter Titian; Titus is of uncertain, perhaps Latin, origin.
Lieke: Dutch pet form of Elisabeth or of names starting with Lie-, such as Liesbeth. Ultimately from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Samir: Arabic, meaning 'companion in evening conversation' or 'entertaining companion'. Also used in South Asia and the Balkans.
Beau: French and English word meaning 'handsome' or 'beautiful', used as a given name for boys; from Latin bellus.
Hind: Arabic, a classical women's name, traditionally explained as 'a group of camels'. Borne by early Islamic-era women.
Efe: Turkish, meaning 'elder brother' or 'brave, respected man'. Also a name among the Yoruba and Edo in Nigeria, where it relates to wealth.
Talha: Arabic, the name of a tree, the acacia (talh). Borne by Talha ibn Ubaydullah, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
Isabel: Spanish, Portuguese and English form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
Marlon: Probably from a French surname, possibly a diminutive of Merle or Marle. Popularised by the actor Marlon Brando.
Aleksander: Polish, Scandinavian and Baltic form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Wies: Dutch short form of Louise (Wies) or of Matthias and Lodewijk. Origin of the pet form is Germanic, 'famous warrior'.
Sil: Dutch short form of Silvester or Silvia, from Latin silva 'forest'; sometimes of Silas.
Robine: Dutch feminine form of Robin, itself a pet form of Robert, from Germanic 'bright fame'.
Lisandro: Spanish form of Lysander, from Greek Lysandros, 'liberator of men'.
Hayat: Arabic, meaning 'life'. Used for girls across the Arabic-speaking world, also in Turkey.
Olga: Slavic form of Old Norse Helga, 'holy, blessed'. Borne by Saint Olga of Kyiv.
Arman: Armenian and Persian, with meanings such as 'wish, dream, aspiration'. Also a Kazakh name.
Elvira: Spanish, of Germanic Visigothic origin, possibly 'true, faithful' or 'elf-counsel'. The etymology is uncertain.
Aissatou: West African form of Aisha (Fulani, Wolof, Mandinka), from Arabic 'alive, living'.
Mariame: West African (French-speaking) form of Mariam or Maryam, the Arabic form of Mary. Meaning of Mary is uncertain, possibly 'beloved'.
Alvaro: Spanish and Portuguese, probably from Visigothic Alfher, 'elf army' or 'all-guard'. Origin uncertain.
Alaa: Arabic, meaning 'excellence, nobility' or 'blessings, gifts'. Used for both sexes in the Arab world.
Zack: English short form of Zachary, from Hebrew Zekharyah, 'the Lord remembers'.
Nao: Japanese, with meanings depending on the characters, such as 'honest' or 'straight'. Also a Spanish and Catalan word for 'ship'.
Milas: Probably a variant of Milan or Miles, possibly Slavic mil 'dear, gracious'. Also a Turkish town. Origin uncertain.
Ammar: Arabic, meaning 'long-lived' or 'devout builder'. Borne by Ammar ibn Yasir, a companion of the Prophet.
Vigo: Probably Germanic, from wig 'battle'. Also a Spanish city. Used in Scandinavia as a short form of Viggo.
Loqman: Arabic Luqman, a wise man in the Quran with a chapter named after him. Meaning is uncertain.
Maho: Japanese, with meanings depending on the characters, often 'true sail' or similar. A Japanese girls' name that is rare for boys in Belgium; origin uncertain here.
Ivar: Old Norse Ívarr, from yr 'yew, bow' and herr 'army'. A Scandinavian name.
Joudia: Probably an Arabic name from jawda or judi, meaning 'generosity' or 'excellence'. Origin uncertain.
Timaël: Modern French invented name, probably blending Timothée with the -aël ending as in Mickaël. Origin uncertain.
Layal: Arabic, plural of layl 'night', so 'nights'. Used mainly for girls in Lebanon and Syria.
Loa: Probably a modern form of Lou or Loïs, or from Hawaiian and Polynesian loa 'long'. Origin uncertain.
Octavia: Latin feminine of Octavius, from octavus 'eighth'.
Lío: Spanish variant of Leo, from Latin leo 'lion'. Also Spanish for 'mess' as a word.
Niels: Dutch and Danish form of Nicholas, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Jordan: Hebrew, from the River Jordan, 'to flow down'. Used for both sexes in Europe and America.
Isabelle: French form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
Maeva: Tahitian, meaning 'welcome'. Popular in France since the 1980s.
Grégoire: French form of Gregory, from Greek Gregorios, 'watchful, alert'.
Andrew: English form of Greek Andreas, meaning 'manly, brave'. Saint Andrew was an apostle.
Jeff: English short form of Jeffrey or Geoffrey, from Germanic elements perhaps meaning 'peace' or 'pledge'.
Iman: Arabic, meaning 'faith, belief'. Used mostly for girls, also for boys in some regions.
Andres: Spanish and Estonian form of Andrew, from Greek 'manly, brave'.
Evi: Dutch short form of Eva, from Hebrew Chava, 'life' or 'to live'.
Matis: Variant of Mathis or Matthias, from Greek form of Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Angela: Latin and Italian, from Greek angelos, 'messenger' or 'angel'.
Hanae: Japanese, 'flower blossom'; also an Arabic-based variant of Hana, 'happiness, bliss'. Used in Morocco and Belgium for the Arabic sense.
Daniël: Dutch form of Daniel, from Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Assya: Probably a variant of Asia or Arabic Asiya, 'one who heals or comforts'. Asiya was the wife of the Pharaoh in Islamic tradition.
Luiz: Portuguese variant of Luís, from Germanic 'famous warrior' (Louis).
Isaure: French, from Latin Isauria, meaning 'woman from Isauria', a region in Asia Minor. A medieval troubadour name.
Beatrice: Italian and English, from Latin beatrix, 'she who brings happiness'. Associated with Dante's muse.
Jerôme: Variant spelling of Jérôme, French form of Greek Hieronymos, 'sacred name'.
Summer: English word for the season, used as a given name since the 20th century.
Yasir: Arabic, meaning 'easy' or 'wealthy'. Borne by Yasir, father of Ammar ibn Yasir.
Anya: Russian pet form of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, 'grace, favour'. Also used in India with other meanings.
Ophélia: French form of Ophelia, probably from Greek ophelos 'help, advantage'. Famous from Shakespeare's Hamlet.
Emi: Japanese, with meanings such as 'beautiful blessing' or 'smile', depending on the characters. Also a short form of Emily.
Lion: From the English and Dutch word for the animal, ultimately Greek leon. Also a German form related to Leo.
Nelia: Probably a short form of Cornelia, from Latin Cornelius, perhaps 'horn'. Also used in Slavic languages. Origin uncertain.
Amilia: Variant of Amelia or Emilia, from Latin Aemilius, 'rival', with Germanic influence from amal 'work'.
Ayat: Arabic, plural of aya, meaning 'signs' or 'verses' of the Quran.
Aboubacar: West African form of Abu Bakr, Arabic for 'father of the young camel'. Abu Bakr was the first caliph.
Tilda: Short form of Matilda, from Germanic 'mighty in battle'.
Ophelia: Probably from Greek ophelos, 'help, advantage'. Coined in Renaissance literature and made famous by Shakespeare's Hamlet.
Ceriel: Dutch short form of Cyriel, from Greek Kyrillos, 'lordly'. Common in Flanders.
Kimia: Persian, from Arabic 'alchemy'; also meaning 'precious, rare'.
Moos: Dutch short form of Mozes (Moses), probably from Egyptian mose 'child'; also pet form of Matthias.
Élisabeth: French form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
Masa: Several origins: Japanese 'correct, good'; Slavic short form of Marija; Arabic 'diamond'. Origin uncertain.
Pollie: Probably a variant of Polly, an English pet form of Molly and Mary. Origin of Mary uncertain, possibly 'beloved'.
Lavin: Possibly Kurdish, meaning 'beloved' or 'lover'. Also an Irish surname. Origin uncertain.
Maylon: Modern coined name, probably blending May or Mason with the ending -lon, as in Marlon. Origin uncertain.
Lynao: Modern coined name, probably an invented variant of Lynn or Nao. Origin uncertain.
Kawtar: Arabic Kawthar, 'abundance'. The name of a river in paradise and a chapter of the Quran.
Josse: French and Dutch form of Judoc, a Breton saint's name meaning 'lord' (Celtic iudoc, 'lord').
Marie-Julie: French compound of Marie, probably Hebrew 'beloved', and Julie, from Latin Julius.
Stig: Scandinavian, from Old Norse stígr, 'path, wanderer'.
Alexine: French feminine diminutive of Alexis, from Greek 'defender'.
Hakim: Arabic, meaning 'wise' or 'judge'. Also 'doctor' in some usage.
Miley: Probably English, from the pet name of Miles or Smiley. Popularised by singer Miley Cyrus, whose name was originally Smiley.
Delia: Latin, 'of Delos', an epithet of Artemis. Also a short form of Cordelia or Bedelia.
Fé: Spanish and Portuguese for 'faith'; used as a short form of Fedora or Feliciana.
Clovis: French form of Frankish Chlodowig, 'famous in battle'. The same root gave Louis.
Lucca: Italian, from the city of Lucca or a form of Luca (Luke), from Greek Loukas, 'from Lucania'.
Dion: Short form of Dionysius, from Greek, 'follower of Dionysos'.
Melody: English, from Greek melodia, 'singing of songs'.
Lian: Chinese 'lotus' or 'graceful'; also Hebrew 'my God answered' and a modern invention. Origin varies by family.
Jule: German and Dutch short form of Julia or Juliane, from Latin Julius.
Yazid: Arabic, meaning 'he increases' or 'grows'. Borne by an Umayyad caliph.
Siana: Probably a modern variant of Sianna or Sian, Welsh form of Jane, 'God is gracious'. Origin uncertain.
Binta: West African, a Fulani and Mandinka form of Arabic bint, 'daughter'; used as a short form of Fatima's name.
Bogdan: Slavic, from bog 'God' and dan 'given', so 'God-given'.
Pien: Dutch pet form of Alpien or Jacoba or Sophie, probably a short form of Pieternella. Origin uncertain.
Liyah: Variant of Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'. Also a modern form of Aaliyah, 'exalted'.
Aurèle: French form of Aurelius, a Roman family name from Latin aureus, 'golden'.
Zaya: Probably Mongolian zaya 'fate, destiny', or an Arabic/Hebrew variant of Zayyah. Origin uncertain.
Mabel: English, a medieval short form of Amabel, from Latin amabilis, 'lovable'.
Maëlan: Breton-style modern name, likely from Maël, Celtic 'prince', with the suffix -an. Origin uncertain.
Asaf: Hebrew 'he gathered' (Asaph); also Arabic 'forgiving'. Asaph was a psalmist.
Mylann: Modern coined name, probably a respelling of Milan or Mylan. Origin uncertain.
Otte: Dutch and Frisian form of Otto, Germanic aud 'wealth, fortune'. Also a Frisian girls' name here.
Alaïa: Probably a variant of Alaya or Alaia, perhaps Arabic 'exalted' or Basque. Famous through fashion designer Azzedine Alaïa. Origin uncertain.
Énora: Breton, a form of Honora, from Latin honor, 'honour'. Saint Énora is venerated in Brittany.
Asil: Arabic, meaning 'of noble origin, authentic'. Also Turkish.
Azlan: Turkish and Malay, from Turkic arslan 'lion'.
Roel: Dutch short form of Roeland (Roland) or Rudolf, from Germanic 'fame' and 'wolf'.
Erwan: Breton form of Yves or Ervoan, from Celtic roots probably 'yew'. Common in Brittany.
Tiana: Probably a short form of Tatiana, or a modern coined name. Popularised by Disney's Tiana. Origin uncertain.
Tara: Irish, from Teamhair, 'hill of the king'; also Sanskrit 'star'.
Melis: Turkish, probably from Greek melissa, 'honey bee', or Melissa. Also a Dutch short form of Melisse.
Anwar: Arabic, meaning 'more luminous, brighter', plural of nur 'light'.
Adel: Arabic 'just'; also German 'noble' from Germanic adal. Used for both sexes.
Vito: Italian and Spanish, from Latin Vitus, 'life' or 'alive'. Borne by Saint Vitus.
Nathaniel: Hebrew, 'God has given'. A biblical name for an apostle.
Soulaymane: North African French spelling of Sulayman, the Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew 'peace'.
Hanaé: Variant of Hanae; Japanese 'flower blossom' or Arabic Hana 'happiness'. Used in French-speaking regions.
Azad: Persian and Kurdish, meaning 'free'. A Turkish and Indian name as well.
Onno: Dutch and Frisian, a short form of Otto or Onno from Germanic aud 'wealth'.
Alexandros: Greek form of Alexander, 'defender of men'.
Zola: Zulu 'calm, tranquil'; also an Italian surname of the writer Émile Zola. Origin varies.
Balthazar: From Babylonian Belshazzar, 'Bel protect the king', later one of the three Magi in Christian tradition.
Mayar: Probably Arabic Mayar, said to mean 'light' or 'serenity', or a Hebrew-based variant of Maya. Origin uncertain.
Pola: Polish short form of Apolonia, from Greek 'belonging to Apollo'. Also a variant of Paula.
Paulo: Portuguese form of Paul, from Latin Paulus, 'small, humble'.
Mayla: Modern name, probably a variant of Maya or Mayla, perhaps from Maya 'water' or May. Origin uncertain.
Roza: Slavic and Turkish form of Rose, from Latin rosa or Germanic 'fame'.
Gael: From Breton Gaël, from Welsh and Celtic root 'generous'. Also the Gaelic people.
Alyah: Variant of Aaliyah, Arabic 'exalted, sublime'. Or Hebrew aliyah 'ascent'.
Miruna: Romanian, probably from Slavic mir 'peace' or Greek myron 'sweet oil'. Origin uncertain.
Abbas: Arabic, meaning 'stern' or 'austere, lion-like'. Borne by an uncle of the Prophet Muhammad.
Iosif: Romanian and Russian form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Zeyna: Variant of Zeynep or Zaina, from Arabic Zaynab, 'fragrant tree' or 'beautiful, graceful'.
Paulette: French diminutive of Paule, feminine of Paul, from Latin 'small'.
Afra: Latin, 'African woman' or 'from Africa'; also Arabic 'white-brown' and Hebrew 'dust'. Saint Afra of Augsburg.
Élie: French form of Elijah, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Nélio: Portuguese and French, probably a variant of Cornelius or Nélio from Greek Helios 'sun'. Origin uncertain.
Artemis: Greek, the goddess of the hunt. Etymology unknown, possibly pre-Greek.
Nahïl: Probably a variant of Arabic Nahil, 'one who drinks from a spring', or 'Nabil'. Origin uncertain.
Rémon: Dutch and French variant of Raymond or Rémy, from Germanic 'wise protector'.
Umay: Turkic, the mother goddess of Turkic mythology; meaning 'womb, placenta'. A Turkish girls' name.
Marit: Scandinavian and Dutch short form of Margareta, from Greek margarites, 'pearl'.
Ilan: Hebrew, 'tree'. Also Basque and Latin-American variants.
Joey: English diminutive of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Nena: Spanish and Slavic pet name meaning 'baby girl' or a short form of Magdalena or Marina. Also a German singer's stage name.
Matthis: Variant of Mathis, a form of Matthias, from Greek form of Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Iliana: Variant of Ileana, Romanian or Greek, probably from Helen 'torch' or Troy (Ilion). Origin uncertain.
Timothé: French form of Timothy, from Greek Timotheos, 'honouring God'.
Driss: North African variant of Idris, an Arabic prophet's name, possibly 'interpreter' or 'studious'.
Jinthe: Dutch variant of Jinte, probably a pet form of Jacinta or Jantine. Origin uncertain.
Artuur: Dutch spelling of Arthur, Celtic possibly 'bear' or Roman Artorius. Origin uncertain.
Joël: Hebrew, 'Yahweh is God'. A biblical prophet.
Finne: Dutch, possibly a form of Finn, 'fair' in Irish Fionn, or 'from Finland'. Used for both sexes in Dutch.
Benthe: Dutch and Frisian, probably from Bente, a Danish form of Benedikta, Latin 'blessed'.
Jakub: Czech, Polish and Slovak form of Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov, 'supplanter'.
Karl: Germanic, from karl 'free man'. Origin of Charles.
Siméon: French form of Simeon, from Hebrew Shim'on, 'he has heard'.
Alae: Probably a variant of Arabic Alaa, 'excellence, nobility'. Used in North Africa.
Mathilda: Latinised form of Germanic Mathilde, 'mighty in battle'.
Giada: Italian for 'jade', the green gemstone; from Spanish piedra de ijada.
Levy: Variant of Levi, Hebrew 'attached, joined'. Also an English surname.
Carlo: Italian form of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Lizzie: English diminutive of Elizabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Abigaël: French form of Abigail, from Hebrew, 'my father is joy'.
Lis: Short form of Elisabeth, or Danish and Dutch for 'lily' (lis, French fleur-de-lis).
Ely: Possibly a short form of Elias or Elijah, 'my God is Yahweh'. Also used for girls as a pet form of Eliane.
Kamélia: French form of Camellia, the flower named after Georg Kamel, a Jesuit botanist.
Adele: Germanic, from adal 'noble'. Italian and English form of Adèle.
Oumayra: Arabic Umayra, a diminutive of Amira, 'princess' or of Umm, a variant meaning 'little princess'.
Rhea: Greek, a Titaness, mother of Zeus; etymology uncertain, possibly 'flow' or 'ground'.
Aybars: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and bars 'tiger, panther'.
Laël: Probably a modern French name from Hebrew El 'God' or a shortening of Raphaël or Gaël. Origin uncertain.
Ceril: Variant of Ceriel or Cyril, from Greek Kyrillos, 'lordly'.
Lidya: Variant of Lydia, Greek, 'woman from Lydia', a region in Asia Minor.
Aden: Irish and Gaelic Aodhán, 'little fire'; also Arabic for 'Eden' or the Yemen port. Used for both sexes.
Yana: Slavic form of Jana (Jane), from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Xavier: From the Basque place name Etxeberri 'new house', via Saint Francis Xavier.
Fabio: Italian, from Latin Fabius, a Roman family name possibly from faba 'bean'.
Arwen: Invented by J. R. R. Tolkien in Sindarin, meaning 'noble maiden'. Also Welsh 'fair, muse'.
Mirko: Slavic and Italian short form of names with mir 'peace', such as Miroslav.
Matt: English short form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
